changelog: - **`clientIp()` no longer trusts `X-Real-IP` at `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=0`** (#2470, the #858 hole one header over). The #858 fix gated `X-Forwarded-For` behind the hop count, but the fall-through read `x-real-ip` unconditionally — so at `0`, documented as "no proxy: trust nothing", a caller rotating `X-Real-IP` got a fresh rate-limit bucket per request and an unbounded key per value. Both proxy headers now sit behind one gate (`clientIpFrom(request, hops)` in `src/lib/clientIp.ts`): at `0` neither is read and every caller is `unknown`, i.e. one shared bucket per limit. Honest traffic is unchanged — without a proxy nothing sets either header, so it already landed there — and production (`1`, behind the reverse proxy) is unaffected; the defect was latent, reachable only at `0`. The rule is pinned by a new unit suite (`scripts/test/client-ip.test.mjs`, 100% lines, floored at 95 in `check-unit-coverage.mjs`), which fails 2/9 against the old gate. The e2e suite depended on the old behaviour (#2159's `floodIp()`/`freshIp()` isolated buckets via `X-Real-IP` under `0`), so the mechanism moved with it: the e2e webServers now run at `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=1`, production's setting, and the helpers send the single-entry `X-Forwarded-For` a one-hop proxy produces. The #858 spoofing test in `e2e/rate-limit.spec.ts` now runs under that same setting against the header shape a proxy would forward — a rotating client-written leftmost entry ahead of a pinned appended one — asserts every request after the fifth is a 429, and adds a control that a different appended peer still gets a 200 (which is also what would catch a webServer quietly back at `0`, where every helper's isolation would silently do nothing). `npm run check:e2e-rate-limits` stays green. No other reader of a client-written IP header exists in `src/`; the `X-Forwarded-Host` readers are behind the #2488 served-host allowlist or are presentation-only.
